(in person at 1916 McAllister) Friday, November 27 (9:30 AM – 11:00 AM) D1 Coffee With Comrades (in person at 2 Clement) Friday, November 27 (9:30 AM – 11:00 AM) D9 Coffee With Comrades (in person at 3188 Mission) Monday, November 30 (7:00 PM – 8:00 PM) Labor Working Group Meeting (zoom and in person at 1916 McAllister) Stop Arming Israel Mobilization AROC, our DSA SF partner in the No Appetite for Apartheid campaign, has put out a call for the Bay Area community to join a mobilization this coming Saturday, November 21st at 12:00 PM at San Francisco Embarcadero Center . This is in response to a call to action put out by the Palestinian labor movement in Gaza and throughout Palestine for the international community to continue to advocate for the Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank that are still enduring immense suffering from the Israeli lead genocide and ethnic cleansing. They are calling for actions to take place around the world from Friday, November 20th to Sunday, November 29th. With this past midterm election, voters clearly sent a message to the US government that the use of our taxpayer money should not be used for military aggression both at home and abroad. This especially applies to stopping support for the Israeli apartheid government and continuing the boycott, divest and sanction movement. Let’s get out and show our support for this mobilization and make it clear once again that we will continue to fight for Palestinian liberation. EWOC Fundamentals of Workplace Organizing — November Session Do you have problems at your workplace or generally have frustrations with the systems governing your communities? Would you like to learn how to talk to people in order to build collective power? Are you interested in discussing organizing strategies with comrades of various organizing levels? If you said “yes” to any of those questions (or are just a radical person), attend our sessions each Sunday of November 3:00 – 4:30 PM for the EWOC Fundamentals of Workplace Organizing course! Emergency Workplace Organizing Committee (EWOC) is a collaboration between national DSA and the United Electrical, Radio & Machine Workers of America (UE) to organize unorganized workplaces and build a distributed, grassroots organizing program to support workers organizing at the workplace. This training course is meant to help you build your union from the ground up alongside workers in your industry. It doesn’t require an organizing background to understand the material, which covers topics including mapping and charting, building an organizing committee, uniting over common concerns, and how to take action. If you’re interested in becoming any level of organizer for EWOC, this course is mandatory. This course will be in-person, with the group watching the EWOC lectures and the discussion activities occurring at the DSA office (1916 McAllister) . If you can’t make all of the sessions, reach out to san-francisco@workerorganizing.org for accommodations. RSVP here EWOC Fundamentals of Working Organizing: Week #2 Reportback The second week of the four-week EWOC Fundamentals training was focused on 1:1 conversations. We watched a recorded session, led by a worker that organized at a chocolate factory in SF and is now a labor lawyer, and another worker currently organizing at Whole Foods. Organizing conversations, or 1:1s are the moments where an organizer builds trust with a co-worker, brings them into organizing, and moves them to take a concrete action. They are natural, but built around a 6-step framework that EWOC recommends – (1) intro and building trust (2) finding out the issues your co-worker cares about (3) agitating around those issues, (4) building a vision of a future and a Plan To Win, (5) inoculation to prepare them for the boss’s response, and (6) a concrete ask or Calling the Question. The facilitators stressed that these steps should not feel transactional, and may take many conversations. Building trust and often socializing before you organize are great first steps, rather than checking the boxes of these 6 steps or projecting your own issues onto your co-worker. After the recorded session, our discussion placed these 1:1 conversations in the context of labor law. All portions of the conversation are legally protected by the NLRA, but that shouldn’t be our focus. The Plan To Win is workers taking collective action together, not necessarily a just a legally certified NLRB election and a contract. The workers at Whole Foods won their union certification vote, but still don’t have a contract, and that’s an intentional tactic by the boss. Beyond that, many of the labor victories of the last century, going back to the 8hr day and 5 day work week, were won by militant unions and ‘illegal’ strikes before the Labor Peace of the NLRA. We ended the session by pairing up and practicing 1:1s with each other, with feedback on what we can improve. Every conversation in every workplace will be different, but there’s a framework, and it’s a concrete skill that we can build and practice together. The next (and last) session will take place on Sunday, November 22nd at 3PM, hosted at 1916 McAllister and we will cover inoculation against the boss. If you’d like to get involved with the SF local chapter of EWOC, reach out the EWOC local at san-francisco@workerorganizing.org or email labor@dsasf.org . EWOC is a standing topic at meetings of the Labor Working group, which are held every fourth Monday at 7:00pm, both in-person at 1916 McAllister and over Zoom—the next one will be Monday November 16th! Anyone is welcome to attend, and we’re always looking for people interested in workplace lead canvassing, organizer trainings, and volunteer outreach. If you’re interested in organizing your workplace and would like to be connected with an EWOC organizer, fill out the request form here .
